Egress

EE-gres · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Egress is the action of going out or leaving a place; an exit.

The old theater's single egress became a serious safety concern once the building's capacity was expanded.

Worked Example

Building inspectors flagged the basement apartment for having no proper egress in case of fire.

Egress refers to a way out or the act of leaving a place -- here, the basement lacked a safe exit route.

How Egress Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

exit

exit: a way out of a place

departure

departure: the act of leaving

Antonyms

entrance

entrance: a way into a place

ingress

ingress: the act of entering or a way in -- the direct opposite of egress

How Strong Is It? — gap → egress → evacuation

gap vs. egress

gap vs. egress: A gap is just a small opening or space, without necessarily functioning as a way out the way an egress does.

evacuation vs. egress

evacuation vs. egress: An evacuation is a full, urgent departure of everyone from a place, a much larger event than a single egress point.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — e- / ex-

prefix — e- / ex-: out, out of (Latin)

root — -gress-

root — -gress-: to step, to walk, to go (Latin gradi)

Put it together

Put it together: Egress comes from Latin e- ('out') plus gradi ('to step, to walk'), literally 'a stepping out.' The same gress- root shows up in many other English words describing different kinds of 'going' -- including the everyday word progress, literally a 'stepping forward.'

Use the root in a new word: progress

Use the root in a new word: progress: After weeks of practice, the team finally began to make real progress toward their championship goal.

Root Check

Word Choice

Egress is a fairly formal or technical word, most often seen in building codes, safety regulations, and legal documents -- in everyday speech, people almost always just say 'exit' instead.
